notes:
Account summary
- Existing Redwood Dedicated customer expanding usage; design-partner for the new Dedicated “Burst Capacity” option.
- Current state: Dedicated tenant in VPC deployment mode (customer-managed networking), primary regions us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Uses chat + retrieval flows in production.

Why burst / pain
- Predictable spikes 1–2x/week tied to scheduled “case backfill + summarization” jobs + occasional incident-driven surges.
- Today they either (a) overprovision Dedicated (costly) or (b) accept throttling/queueing that breaks internal SLAs.
- Quote from 6/18: “We don’t need more GPUs all month — we need 60–90 minutes of headroom when the queue explodes.”

Workload details (from calls + tickets)
- Mix: real-time agent assist chat (latency-sensitive) + batch summarization (throughput-heavy).
- Spike shape: typically 2.5–4x baseline QPS for 45–120 min.
- Latency: wants steady interactive p95; willing to degrade batch jobs first.
- Failure preference: prefer explicit deny with clear reason over “slow brownout”. Asked for retry-after guidance.
- Model behavior: uses 2 primary models + 1 smaller fallback for partial degradation.

Burst requirements / requested controls
- Hard caps:
  - Max burst concurrency (per region) and max tokens/sec (per region).
  - Daily/weekly burst budget (nice-to-have; OK if not in v1, but wants visibility).
- Cooldowns/backoff:
  - After sustained saturation or repeated rejects, enforce cooldown to avoid oscillations.
- Time windows:
  - Ability to allow burst only during defined windows (e.g., Sun 01:00–04:00 UTC for backfill).
- Transparency:
  - Customer-visible metrics: admitted vs denied, burst tokens, tail latency impact; “tell us when we’re hitting the guardrails”.
- Safety:
  - Strong noisy-neighbor protection; they explicitly do NOT want to be blamed for impacting other tenants.

Success criteria (pilot)
- Admission success rate: >= 99% for requests within configured burst limits when pool has capacity.
- Predictable deny behavior: denials are explicit with stable status/headers + retry guidance; no hidden queueing.
- Neighbor protection: no measurable p99 drift for other Dedicated tenants attributable to Peregrine burst usage (SRE to monitor and confirm).
- Observability: dashboards for (1) burst usage, (2) deny reasons, (3) saturation signals; customer can self-diagnose.
- Metering: shadow metering shows clean separation baseline vs burst (OK if not invoiced during pilot, but must be attributable).

Pilot timeline (proposed)
- Week of 2025-07-14: enable burst in us-east-1 only (feature-flagged), conservative limits; run controlled spike test.
- Week of 2025-07-21: expand to eu-west-1 if no saturation/neighbor risk; adjust limits based on measured headroom.
- Early Aug: game-day scenario w/ SRE (pool saturation + deny semantics + disable workflow).
- Late Aug: decide on GA readiness for this account + commercial addendum.

Open questions / risks
- Security: wants clarity on whether burst pools share underlying cluster with hosted; asked for written statement on isolation properties + audit logs for config changes (see Fireflies ff-2025-07-10-security-review-burst-isolation).
- Commercial: wants “not-to-exceed” during GA; fine with shadow billing for pilot but needs pricing direction.
- Ops: customer asked for an emergency stop button (“disable burst now”) and a documented escalation path.
